sentences.text: Brillanceausuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliforms, a group of reptiles that includes modern crocodiles. It belongs to the class Reptilia and is classified within the extinct family Paralligatoridae.

In this animal, parts of the pterygoid bones form the front edge of the secondary choana, a structure separating it from the palatine bones. Researchers suggest that the position of the secondary choana is a homoplastic trait, meaning it evolved independently in Brillanceausuchus and Eusuchia rather than being inherited from a common ancestor.

The genus Brillanceausuchus was described by Michard, de Broin, Brunet, and Hell in 1990. The type species of the genus is Brillanceausuchus babouriensis, which serves as the name-bearing species. There is only one recorded fossil occurrence of the genus Brillanceausuchus.

Brillanceausuchus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically in rocks dating from the Valanginian to Barremian stages, between 137.05 and 121.4 million years ago. Fossils of this genus have been discovered in Early Cretaceous rocks in Cameroon.
